title: Cell-level energy budget and test basis for the MiniNode '>2-year' battery claim
question: What do peer-reviewed low-current/low-temperature alkaline-cell characterisation studies, IEC 60086-2 test conditions and manufacturer data establish about usable capacity, self-discharge, passivation and voltage delay of 2×AA alkaline cells at roughly 10–50 µA average drain and a 1.8–2.0 V cut-off, and what test basis makes the MiniNode P1 'credible >2-year practical battery path' a defensible product claim rather than a nameplate extrapolation?
why_now: The same handoff fixes P1 as <50 µA average and a 'credible >2-year practical battery path, not a marketing claim until validated', but gives no cell derating, temperature range or test standard. In an unheated shed the nameplate arithmetic can overstate life, and Project principle 7 forbids performance values with false precision.
real_world_anchor: 2×AA alkaline cell usable capacity, self-discharge and low-temperature derating at microamp drains (IEC 60086-2 and peer-reviewed characterisation studies); nRF54L15 1.8–3.6 V supply range
novelty_reason: The prior MiniNode topic covers sensor/enclosure metrology, not the power subsystem. This gap audits the distinct P1 energy-budget claim: usable cell capacity, temperature derating and test standard. It adds a decision-relevant boundary that the prior topic did not address.
